title: `corr`: shared state; NaN for one pair or zero variance
verdict: dp_xy / sqrt(dp_xx · dp_yy); NaN where the reference is NULL; no clamp
description: `PearsonState` returns `dp_xy / sqrt(dp_xx * dp_yy)` if `dp_xx * dp_yy > 0`, else NaN: one pair or a zero variance is NaN. Not clamped to [-1, 1]. `dp_xx * dp_yy` can overflow or underflow before the square root.
No pairs: null in the streaming reducer; the in-memory path (`polars-ops` `cov.rs`) returns NaN.
reference: `AggFn.corr` (`corrOf`): NULL for fewer than two pairs, or for a side whose values are all equal; else the co-deviation sum by the square root of the product of the two squared-deviation sums. It is not clamped to [-1, 1]. Engines may differ in the last bits (#54) until #85 bounds the error.
Where the reference is NULL (one pair, a constant side), Polars gives NaN.
